In a name of the form SECTION.KEY, the key is the part after the last dot, and a name without a dot is a key in the unnamed section

criteria.baseline: it must pass on the input snapshot, as a regression guard; interlock saw it pass there (run run-ad760849d5544f81)

goal:
`kvconf get` cannot read a key in a section whose name contains a dot. With this file:

```
[db.eu]
host = db1.example.org
```

`go run ./cmd/kvconf get app.conf db.eu.host` prints `kvconf: no section "db"` instead of `db1.example.org`.

Section names may contain dots; keys never do. So in a name of the form `SECTION.KEY`, the key is the part after the last dot: `db.eu.host` is the key `host` in the section `db.eu`. A name without a dot is a key in the unnamed section.

`checks/dotted.sh` reproduces the problem. The tests run with `go test ./...`.

previous_result.summary:
`kvconf get app.conf db.eu.host` now returns `db1.example.org`. The name is split at the last dot, so `db.eu.host` is the key `host` in the section `db.eu`.

The bug was in two places that each split `SECTION.KEY` at the first dot: `Config.Lookup` in `config.go` and `splitName` in `cmd/kvconf/main.go`. Both now split at the last dot, and a name with no dot is still a key in the unnamed section. I also added `TestLookupDottedSection` in `parser_test.go` and a note about dotted section names in `README.md`.

interlock ran `checks/dotted.sh` (repro) and `go test ./...` (regression) on the final files, and both pass. I recorded claims for all three criteria. `spec` rests on `TestLookupDottedSection`, which only exercises `Lookup`, not the CLI. The CLI path is covered by the `checks/dotted.sh` run.
